title: Agent feedback from using CTL branch-store merge tooling during the D(Dic_12) Yasui trace merge

scope.question: Record constructive user/agent feedback after using the newly adopted CTL branch-store merge tooling to merge the D(Dic_12) Yasui a=1 compact-trace CTL objects over main's provider/tooling adoption root.
scope.claim_boundary: This is process feedback for upstream tooling. It does not assert mathematical content, CTL kernel semantics, or a new research result.
scope.source_event: No-ff merge of main commit b0d82ac into codex/dic12-yasui-a1-ctl-trace, with target root ctlobj-sha256:04ee89a9005c... and incoming root ctlobj-sha256:c99490bce09c...
scope.outcome: The tooling correctly produced a full-transplant plan with 7 auto-admit bindings and no logical conflicts, transplanted those bindings onto the main provider-adoption root, and verify.py passed at root ctlobj-sha256:578523fe5aef...

what_worked_well: The runbook vocabulary of target/incoming/base made the CTL merge safer than thinking in Git ours/theirs terms.
The tool correctly classified the merge as full-transplant with auto-admit=7 and conflict=0.
The transplant command produced a clean target-side root and a merge manifest that explains each transplanted binding.
manifest-plan was very helpful for catching that the incoming sidecar manifests were branch-local and should not be kept as target-current manifests.
After cleanup, verify.py accepted the final root and provider adoption policy.

constructive_complaints.issue: runbook cannot start from a normal Git conflict state where ctl-dogfood/refs/main.json contains conflict markers.
constructive_complaints.impact: The agent had to manually restore the target-side ref before the CTL tool could even read the store. This feels backwards precisely when the tool is most needed.
constructive_complaints.suggestion: Add a conflict-state mode that accepts explicit --main-root and --incoming-root without loading refs/main.json first, or print a safe command that writes a temporary target ref from the chosen target root.

constructive_complaints.issue: The runbook's printed transplant command omitted --incoming-root even though the runbook itself was invoked with an explicit incoming root.
constructive_complaints.impact: In a same-worktree conflict resolution, refs/main.json had already been restored to the target root, so running the printed command literally would risk defaulting incoming-root to the target ref instead of the intended incoming branch root.
constructive_complaints.suggestion: When runbook was called with explicit roots, echo those explicit roots in every generated follow-up command.

constructive_complaints.issue: manifest-plan output is too verbose for the common case.
constructive_complaints.impact: The useful information was seven branch-local warnings, but it was buried among more than a hundred reachable historical manifests.
constructive_complaints.suggestion: Provide a --problems-only or --actionable-only mode, and include a copy-pastable cleanup list for branch-local sidecar manifests that should be omitted.

constructive_complaints.issue: write operations and verify have long silent periods.
constructive_complaints.impact: Each admission/transplant/verify step can take tens of seconds with no progress indicator, making it hard for an agent to tell whether it is replaying correctly or stuck.
constructive_complaints.suggestion: Emit progress by phase: load store, find base, classify transitions, write batch N/M, replay verify N/M. A JSON event stream mode would be ideal for agents.

constructive_complaints.issue: The final verify JSON reports bootstrap ctl_meta_commit separately from provider.current_ctl_meta_commit, which is easy to misread.
constructive_complaints.impact: A human can see provider.mode=admitted-provider-adoption, but the top-level ctl_meta_commit still shows the old bootstrap commit, creating a momentary false alarm.
constructive_complaints.suggestion: Rename the top-level field to bootstrap_ctl_meta_commit or add current_provider_commit at top level.

constructive_complaints.issue: The tool explains that incoming manifests are branch-local, but not what should happen to already-tracked incoming manifest files during the Git merge.
constructive_complaints.impact: The agent had to infer that those files should be deleted from the final merge tree and replaced by the generated merge manifest.
constructive_complaints.suggestion: Have manifest-plan print explicit Git-resolution guidance: keep historical target manifests, remove listed branch-local incoming manifests from final tree, add generated merge manifest.

overall_assessment.verdict: The new tooling is a substantial safety improvement and did prevent a bad refs/main.json side-choice merge. The remaining pain is mostly agent UX around conflict-state bootstrap, command echoing, and actionable cleanup.
overall_assessment.priority_request: Make runbook usable directly from a Git conflict state with explicit roots, and ensure generated commands preserve the exact roots used for planning.
